title: One actionable metric per stage, with a sourced line in the sand
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Which single metric the plan should move now, how its target is sourced, and how to read it by cohort rather than in aggregate.
applies_when: Plan names a North Star or target
Owner reports cumulative or vanity numbers
exclusions: No numbers at all yet (set a baseline period first)
required_inputs: The metric's numerator, denominator and period
Target source: business-model maths, owner baseline, or dated outside figure
evidence_requirements: whether it is cumulative or per period
business-model maths that implies a required value, if available
the owner's own trend for the metric
customer start dates and activity or payments by month
at least 3 cohorts with 3+ complete months for a survival read
missing_data_behavior: No baseline: first period sets it; no target.
Cohorts below the minimum: aggregate read labelled weak.

decision_branches.if: Metric is cumulative (total to date, list size)
decision_branches.then: Replace with a rate or per-period count.
Inventory metrics allowed when paired with revenue per 1,000.

decision_branches.if: Target taken from a book benchmark
decision_branches.then: Label it dated outside context; prefer the owner's own baseline.

implementation_steps: List the 3-5 metrics the owner watches.
For each, write the action it would trigger if it rose or fell.
Convert cumulative counts to period flows or rates.
Pair each outcome with the paired metric that can move against it (conversion with order value; signups with activation).
Pick the metric that answers it.
Write the line and its source (model maths, own baseline, or dated external norm).
Compute churn by cohort in code.
dependencies: a stated business model (what the business is paid for)
payments or usage data connected (convex computeCohorts) or an owner export
metrics: share of signups active in the period
cohort retention by month of age
guardrails: Each target carries its source tag.
Averages across cohorts of very different size are not used.
never accept an all-time count as progress
show count and denominator with any rate
record every line change with a reason and date
alternatives_when_constrained: no analytics connected: use the owner's own period counts (bookings this month) as the outcome, labelled self-reported
no tracking: owner tallies the metric by hand weekly; or ClimbOS measures a baseline week first
no billing connection: owner's reported monthly churn, labelled self-reported; or a manual list of customers by start month
stop_conditions: review when the business model or stage changes
flat for 3+ readings below the line: change strategy or metric
line changed twice without new evidence: stop and review
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Media and UGC businesses where attention is the inventory (BK12-F23).
Rates on tiny denominators look precise but are fragile (Book 12 §4: show counts beside percentages).
Single-metric focus can hide harm (refunds, churn); pair it with guardrails (Book 12 §1; BK06 OEC).
Lines borrowed from 2013 aggregates mislead small businesses.

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: warn when a North Star or play outcome is a cumulative or all-time count ('total', 'cumulative', 'all-time', 'to date', 'list size'); suggest the per-period flow or rate.

proposed: for media_creator businesses monetised by impressions or sponsorships, allow inventory metrics as the North Star only when the plan pairs them with revenue per 1,000 (computed in code) and an audience-churn reading.
proposed: when three consecutive weekly readings show diminishing gains below the line, the plan suggests switching metric or strategy rather than more of the same.

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: every North Star target carries a source tag: 'model' (computed from goal and price in code), 'owner baseline', or 'external, dated' (with year); external dated targets are shown as orientation and never drive a pass/fail verdict.
proposed: churn shown to owners states its type (paid vs free; customer vs revenue) and denominator method.

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed: when computeCohorts has 3+ cohorts with 3+ complete months, diagnose() uses observed cohort retention for the retention reading and labels the source; owner-typed churn is the fallback.

reconciliation_note: Duplicates BRP-18 on cohorts; adds the vanity filter and target sourcing.
